# Input Checkbox — Accessibility Issues

> Generated by accessibility-auditor. Resolve these issues before using this component in production.

## No visible focus indicator when `opacity: 0` input receives focus

**File:** `input-checkbox.component.scss`, lines 22–29
**WCAG criterion:** 2.4.11 Focus Appearance (Level AA, WCAG 2.2) / 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA, WCAG 2.1)
**Problem:** The projected `<input type="checkbox">` is positioned absolutely with `opacity: 0` to hide the native control while keeping it in the accessibility tree. However, the component SCSS defines no `:focus` or `:focus-visible` rule that redirects the focus ring to the visible `.c-input-checkbox__checker` element. If the application's global CSS reset suppresses `outline` on inputs (a common pattern), keyboard users will receive no visible focus indicator when tabbing to the checkbox, failing both WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.11.
**Recommendation:** Add a `:focus-visible` rule inside the component that applies a visible outline or border to `.c-input-checkbox__checker` when the projected input is focused, for example:

```scss
::ng-deep input[type="checkbox"]:focus-visible ~ .c-input-checkbox__checker,
&:has(input[type="checkbox"]:focus-visible) .c-input-checkbox__checker {
  outline: 2px solid var(--color-quaternary);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Variant `switch` does not expose `role="switch"` to assistive technologies

**File:** `input-checkbox.component.ts` / `input-checkbox.stories.ts`
**WCAG criterion:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)
**Problem:** When `variant="switch"` is used, the component renders a visual toggle switch, but the underlying projected `<input type="checkbox">` retains its default checkbox role. ARIA 1.2 defines `role="switch"` specifically for toggle controls whose state is on/off. Screen readers will announce this control as "checkbox" rather than "switch", which misrepresents the semantic intent and may confuse users relying on assistive technologies.
**Recommendation:** When using `variant="switch"`, the consumer must add `role="switch"` directly to the projected `<input>` element:

```html
<corp-input-checkbox variant="switch">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" name="notifications" id="notifications" />
  Enable notifications
</corp-input-checkbox>
```

Alternatively, the component could detect the `switch` variant and apply `role="switch"` programmatically via a `ContentChild` reference, but that would require a deeper refactor.
